Team —

Attaching the latest pipeline forecast and heatmap (see attachments). We need to lock the reserve-sizing asks for the upcoming deals that are in late-stage Q4 closes so Infra can map to GPU types and Finance can validate spend profile. High level asks: 

- Ben: confirm the committed budget band and any flexibility on short-term burst credits for pilots.
- Karthik: map the top 6 deals to SKU types (A100 vs H100), and note any cases where quantization or ephemeral CPU inference could reduce reserved slots.
- Jordan: call out any upcoming billing/contract timing constraints that would impact when we should provision capacity.

Quick notes from pipeline: Acme AI pilot is expected to ramp from 1k tokens/min to 12k tokens/min over 6 weeks once they hit production (see row in pipeline sheet). We should treat the first 2 weeks as canary traffic and keep a 20% safety margin on reserved slots.

Please reply with updates by EOD Mon 12/7 so I can consolidate for the Dec 11 ops sync with Infra and Ops (I put the invite on calendar).

Attachments: 2026-12-10_pipeline_forecast.xlsx, deal_heatmap_Q4.pdf

Thanks —
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Fleet sizing handoff: week of Dec 11 — action items

Laura —

Quick finance view: we have three deal bands for Q4 closes that matter for reserve sizing:

- Tier A (>$750k ARR annualized): finance will greenlight a 12-month reserved commitment; expect billing to start within 30 days of contract signature.
- Tier B ($250k–$750k): flexible on 3–6 month commits; we can apply limited burst credits for first 30 days.
- Tier C (<$250k): recommend pay-as-you-go until production ROI is proven.

For Acme (Tier B in pipeline sheet), we can approve up to 30% of the pilot cost as temporary burst credits; anything beyond that needs AM/RevOps sign-off. I attached the pricing model with run-rate scenarios — use tab "Acme-scenarios" to see monthly impact.

Ben
Director, Finance (Cloud Ops)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reserved_capacity_pricing_model_v3.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fleet sizing handoff: week of Dec 11 — action items

Thanks — mapping here's my rough hardware mapping and constraints for the 6 priority deals: 

- Acme AI (pilot -> prod ramp): estimated steady-state across peak windows = equivalent of 4 H100s (fp16), plus 1 H100 buffer for canary. If we use int8 quantization and the customer's lower-latency tolerance, we can reduce to 3 H100-equivalents but must validate quality.
- Nimbus Labs: prefers A100; estimate 6 A100 equivalents for initial commit.
- Orion Health: short burst for inference-heavy ETL (LLM reranking) — prefer ephemeral CPU + 2 A100 reserved for spikes.
- DeltaApps: smaller but long duration — 2 A100 reserved.

Notes on capacity and ops: 
- We have limited H100 headroom in us-west for the Dec 15–Jan 15 window (approx 12 H100-equivalents free). If Acme converts mid-December, we will need to prioritize Tier A deals first or enable cross-region fallback to eu-central.
- Suggest option: schedule a canary provisioning window (48–72 hrs) before full reserved allocation for each pilot to validate perf/metrics.

I'll attach a short runbook snippet in the ops doc but happy to surface exact slot counts if you want them broken down by 4-hr rolling windows.

Karthik
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Laura / team —

Thanks for the clear asks. A few clarifications from Acme's side: 

- Pilot ramp plan: we expect traffic to ramp in three phases (0–2w canary, 2–6w steady ramp, 6+w full production). The token/sec profile for steady ramp is attached in the shared doc (Drive).
- Quality vs cost: our ML team is open to an int8 experiment if Redwood provides guidance on model accuracy delta; we'd like to run that in canary only.
- Contract timing: AM is expecting to sign by Dec 14 if legal finishes the SOW — billing start date targeted Jan 1.

Can we get a short canary window provisioned starting Dec 20? That would give us time to validate and adjust. Happy to be on the Dec 11 ops sync if helpful.

—Elena

elena@acme.ai

All — thanks for the quick turn. Consolidated action items before the ops sync on Monday (Dec 13):

1) Karthik: provision tentative canary window for Acme Dec 20–22 (48 hours). If H100 headroom looks tight, propose cross-region fallback; share exact slot counts by EOD Mon 12/14.
2) Ben: confirm final burst-credit approval for Acme (up to 30% pilot cost) and sign-off on billing start Jan 1 if SOW is signed by 12/14.
3) Jordan/Marissa: ensure AM legal and RevOps timeline is visible — if the SOW slips beyond 12/14 we push provisioning back to Jan.
4) Acme (Elena): share int8 experiment acceptance criteria and a quick eval script we can run during canary.

I'll pull these into the ops agenda and send a one-pager for the Dec 13 meeting. If anyone wants me to split the Acme slot across A100/H100 variants for parallel QA, say so — otherwise we'll prioritize H100 for latency-sensitive routes.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
